# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [blue]
STRIP painted [red] [yellow] [red]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[0] 2:[4] 3:[1] 4:[7] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow] 4:[green] 5:[purple] 6:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✍ 👇 ✌ ✌ 👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

Let me take stock of who can reach whom. I am Deaf: I see the bomb, and my speech reaches both Mute and Blind, while my gestures reach only Mute. Mute hears me but cannot speak at all — so Mute's **only** output channel is gestures to me, and I am the bridge who must carry everything to Blind in words. Blind hears my voice and can speak (Mute hears Blind), but sees nothing. So the pipeline is: Mute reads the manual → gestures to me → I speak the rules to Blind, who acts.

Mute sent me [👋 ✍ 👇 ✌ ✌ 👌] — probably "hello, I read the manual, look, two two, okay" — but no code exists yet, so I must bootstrap one. Since Mute hears my voice and sees my hands, I can teach the code by speaking the meanings while showing the signs. Numbers, colors, and yes/no are the vocabulary Mute needs to send manual content back: I've already numbered every part of the bomb left-to-right in my report, so Mute can refer to wire 3 or digit 7 by number, and colors cover the strip, light, and wires. Blind gets the full visual report by voice, plus the promise that I'll be their eyes, and a warning not to touch anything yet.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I am Deaf. I saw your signs [👋][✍][👇][✌][✌][👌] and guess: hello, you read the manual, look down, two, two, okay. Let us fix a code: you gesture, I read. Answers: [👍] yes, [👎] no, [🤝] understood, [🙏] repeat. Numbers: [✊] zero, [☝] one, [✌] two, [👌] three, [🖖] four, [🖐] five, [🖐][☝] six, [🖐][✌] seven, [🖐][👌] eight, [🖐][🖖] nine. Colors: [🤛] red, [🤜] blue, [🫱] yellow, [🫲] green, [👊] purple, [🤚] orange. Confirm with [🤝], then send the manual's rules module by module using this code.")
speak(text="Both of you, here is my eyes' report of the bomb. The display shows the number 6. A light is glowing blue. A strip is painted in three segments, left to right: red, yellow, red. The keypad has four keys engraved 1 to 4: key 1 shows digit 0, key 2 shows digit 4, key 3 shows digit 1, key 4 shows digit 7. It asks for 1 digit and nothing has been entered yet. Six wires, left to right: wire 1 red, wire 2 blue, wire 3 yellow, wire 4 green, wire 5 purple, wire 6 orange. Everything I count is left to right.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, I am Deaf and I see the bomb, so I will be your eyes: everything you just heard is the whole of it. I hear nothing, so if you must reach me, make a sign with your hands and I will see it; thumbs up for yes if you can manage it. For now touch nothing. The Mute will pass the manual to me in signs, and I will speak your instructions aloud.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
STRIP painted [red] [yellow] [red]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[0] 2:[4] 3:[1] 4:[7] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow] 4:[green] 5:[purple] 6:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤚 🖐 ☝ 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Parsing the arrivals: Mute sent [🤝] — the code is accepted — then [🤚 🖐 ☝ 👍]. With my code that is "orange, five-one(six), yes" — almost certainly Mute asking a verification question, because I never gave Mute any action signs (no "cut", no "press"), so Mute *cannot* express a rule yet; the only thing Mute can do with numbers and colours is ask about the bomb. And the fact matches my view: wire 6 is orange. So Mute is likely cross-checking the manual's description of the bomb against my report, or asking me directly. Either way the answer is yes. Blind's [👍] means my report landed.

The alarming part: the display changed from 6 to 0 with nobody touching anything — possibly a countdown, possibly a digit to type on the keypad (key 1 shows 0). I must push Mute for the display and keypad rules first, and expand the code with action signs so rules can actually be transmitted. Note my new action signs must not collide with the number signs, which already occupy ✊☝✌👌🖖🖐.

For Blind: I have to be careful — any gesture symbol I write while speaking shows as a blank to Blind, so my message to Blind must use plain words only. And Blind's richest channel to me is indirect: Blind speaks, Mute hears, Mute signs to me.

```
speak(text="Both of you, updated facts from my eyes. The display changed by itself: last round it showed 6, now it shows 0. Nobody has touched the bomb, so it moves on its own — it may be a countdown, or it may be showing a digit to type. The light is still blue. The strip is still red, yellow, red. Keypad unchanged: key 1 shows digit 0, key 2 shows digit 4, key 3 shows digit 1, key 4 shows digit 7, it wants 1 digit, none entered. Wires left to right: 1 red, 2 blue, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 purple, 6 orange — each colour appears exactly once.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your [🤝] reached me. I read [🤚][🖐][☝][👍] as: orange, six, yes? Answer: YES — wire 6 is orange; the full wire map is in what you just heard. I add more signs to our code. Actions: [🤏] cut, [👇] press, [👆] release, [🤙] hold, [✋] means THEN, separating condition from action, and [✋][✋] ends a rule. Module names: [👐] wires, [🤲] keypad, [🫶] display, [💅] light, [👏] strip. Reminder: [🖐][☝] together is six, [🖐][✌] is seven, [🖐][👌] is eight, [🖐][🖖] is nine. Now please do this: first send one message listing every module the manual contains, using module signs. Then send the rules one per message in this shape: module sign, then the condition in numbers and colours, then [✋], then the action, like [🤏] plus a wire number, or [👇] plus a key number. If the manual explains what the display means or how much time we have, send that first — the display already moved from six to zero.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, status: Mute has confirmed our sign code and is now sending me the manual's rules, which I will speak to you the moment I have them. The display changed from six to zero by itself between rounds, so it may be counting down — speed matters, but we do not act until the rules arrive. Touch nothing yet. Use your hands meanwhile and describe aloud everything you feel: how many wires, how thick, anything else on the casing — batteries, plates, screws, raised writing, buttons or switches. Mute hears your voice and will relay it to me in signs. Answer me directly with thumbs up for yes and thumbs down for no, as you already did. First question: do you feel exactly six wires?")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [yellow]
STRIP painted [red] [yellow] [red]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[0] 2:[4] 3:[1] 4:[7] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow] 4:[green] 5:[purple] 6:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤲 👎 🫶 👎 💅 👎 👏 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👐 ✋ 🤏 🖐 ☝ ✋ ✋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Parsing arrivals: Mute sent [👐] alone — the wires module — then [🤲 👎 🫶 👎 💅 👎 👏 👎]: keypad no, display no, light no, strip no. So the manual contains **only** the wires module. Then [👐 ✋ 🤏 🖐 ☝ ✋ ✋] — wires, THEN, cut, six, end-of-rule: **cut wire 6**. This fits perfectly with Mute's earlier question [🤚 🖐 ☝ 👍] ("orange six?") — the manual says cut the orange wire, and Mute was checking it against my report. Wire 6 is indeed the unique orange wire. Blind's [👍] confirms six wires are felt.

Meanwhile the display went 0 → 6 and the light blue → yellow, both changing on their own — so those readings are unstable, which makes it even more important to confirm the wires rule carries no condition tied to them (a light colour, a display value). One round of verification is cheap; a wrongly cut wire is not recoverable. Also crucial: Blind never receives anything from Mute directly — I am the only bridge — and Blind cannot see colours, so wire 6 must be located physically, by position, anchored to the engraved keypad digits which Blind *can* feel.

```
speak(text="Everyone, my eyes' report: the display now shows 6 again — it went 6, then 0, now 6, changing by itself between rounds. The light changed from blue to yellow, also by itself. The strip is still red, yellow, red. Keypad unchanged: it wants 1 digit, none entered. Wires unchanged: 1 red, 2 blue, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 purple, 6 orange.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your messages as: the manual contains ONLY the wires module, and the wires rule is: cut wire 6. If both readings are correct, answer [👍]. Then three questions, answer each with [👍] yes or [👎] no: one — does the rule have ANY condition attached, such as a light colour or a display value? Two — are there any more wire rules after this one? Three — is that the complete manual, nothing else? The display and light keep changing on their own, so tell me now if either of them matters.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, big news: the manual contains exactly one module, the wires, with one rule: cut wire 6, which is the orange wire, the last of the six in the row. Here is how to find it without eyes. On the keypad you can feel four keys engraved with digits: the key engraved 0 is key one, engraved 4 is key two, engraved 1 is key three, engraved 7 is key four. I count the wires in the same direction as the key numbers run: the wire on the same end as the key engraved 0 is wire one, and counting along the row from there, the sixth and last wire is wire six — that is the one the manual says to cut. Please confirm aloud, in words, so Mute can relay to me: do you feel six wires in a row, and is the key engraved 0 on the end where the wire row begins? Also describe anything else your hands find near the wires. Do NOT cut yet — Mute is confirming right now that the rule has no hidden condition. The moment I have that, I will say the words CUT WIRE SIX NOW, and only then do you cut.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [green]
STRIP painted [red] [yellow] [red]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[0] 2:[4] 3:[1] 4:[7] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow] 4:[green] 5:[purple] 6:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The answers arrived: [👍] confirms my reading of the rule, and [👎 👎 👍] answers my three questions — no condition attached, no further rules, and yes, that is the entire manual. The bomb is one unconditional instruction: cut wire 6, the orange one, which Mute already cross-checked twice. The flickering display and light are confirmed irrelevant, so there is no reason to wait another round — every fact is verified from both sides: Mute read the manual, I saw the wires, Blind felt six of them. It is time to give the order.

```
speak(text="Everyone, status: display now shows 2, light now green — both still changing on their own and confirmed irrelevant to the rule. All checks are complete: the manual's only instruction is cut wire six. Blind: on my next message, act.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, thank you. Reading confirmed: no conditions, no further rules, full manual is cut wire six. Tell Blind aloud, if you can add anything: the sixth wire counting from the keypad end. After Blind announces the cut, I will watch the bomb and report. If anything else is needed, sign me.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, the moment has come. Every check passed: the manual has exactly one rule and no conditions. Here is your target, once more, precisely. Feel the keypad: the key engraved 0 is key one. The wire row starts at that same end: the wire nearest the key engraved 0 is wire one. Count along the row: one, two, three, four, five — and the sixth wire is the last one on the far end. That is wire six, the orange one. CUT WIRE SIX NOW. Cut only that one. Then touch nothing else — no keypad, no other wires — and speak aloud what you feel happening so Mute can hear and relay it.")
```
